articleTitle: VERA Observations of H$_2$O Maser Sources in Three Massive Star-Forming Regions and Galactic Rotation Measurements
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the results of VLBI observations of three H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>O maser sources in massive star-forming regions: IRAS 06058+2138, IRAS 19213+1723, and AFGL 2789. We determined the annual parallaxes and proper motions for these sources by a phase-referencing method. The estimated distances to IRAS 06058+2138 and AFGL 2789 are 1.76<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.11 kpc and 3.07<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.30 kpc, which are located in the Perseus spiral arm. The distance to IRAS 19213+1723 is 3.98<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.57 kpc, placing it in the Carina–Sagittarius arm. With estimated 3-dimensional velocity components, we have shown that the galactic rotation curve is flat in the range of 6.4 kpc <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\le R \le$</tex> 13 kpc as combining with S 269, which was observed with VERA. We have also found that the overall rotation curve of the Galaxy do not depend on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Theta_0$</tex>. The maser sources also show deviations from flat rotation curves by a few kilometers per second. We discuss possible reasons for these peculiar motions.

articleTitle: Errata: Unified Rotation Curve of the Galaxy — Decomposition into de Vaucouleurs Bulge, Disk, Dark Halo, and the 9-kpc Rotation Dip —
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

articleTitle: In-Orbit Performance of the MAXI/SSC onboard the ISS
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report here the in-orbit performance of the CCD camera (MAXI/SSC) onboard the International Space Station (ISS). It was commissioned in 2009 August. This is the first all-sky survey mission employing X-ray CCDs. It consists of 32 CCDs, each of which is 1 inch square. It is a slit camera with a field of view of 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ\!\!\!.$</tex>5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 90<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex>, and scans the sky as the rotation of the ISS. The CCD on the SSC is cooled down to the working temperature around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>60<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex>C by the combination of a peltier cooler, a loop heat pipe and a radiator. The standard observation mode of the CCD is in a parallel sum mode (64-binning). The CCD functions properly, although it suffers an edge glow when the Sun is near the field of view (FOV), which reduces the observation efficiency of the SSC down to about 30%. The performance of the CCD is continuously monitored both by the Mn-K X-rays and by the Cu-K X-rays. There are many sources detected, not only point sources, but extended sources. Due to the lack of an effective observation time, we need more observation time to obtain an extended emission analysis extraction process.

articleTitle: VLBI Monitoring of 3C 84 (NGC 1275) in Early Phase of the 2005 Outburst
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Multi-epoch Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) study of a sub-pc scale jet of 3C 84 is presented. We carried out 14-epoch VLBI observations during 2006–2009 with the Japanese VLBI Network and the VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry, immediately following a radio outburst that began in 2005. We confirmed that the outburst was associated with the central <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim1$</tex> pc core, accompanying the emergence of a new component. This is striking evidence of the recurrence of jet activity. The new component became brighter during 2008, in contrast to constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray emission that was observed with the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope during the same time. We found that the projected speed of the new component was 0.23<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ c$</tex> from 2007/297 (2007 October 24) to 2009/114 (2009 April 24). The direction of movement of this component differs from that of the pre-existing component by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>40<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex>. This was the first measurement of the kinematics of a sub-pc jet in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray active phase. A possible detection of jet deceleration and the jet kinematics in connection with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray emission is discussed.

articleTitle: Ca II K Spectral Study of an Emerging Flux Region using the Domeless Solar Telescope in Hida Observatory
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A cooperative observation with Hida Observatory and the Hinode satellite was performed on an emerging flux region. Successive Ca II K spectro-heliograms of the emerging flux region were taken by the Domeless Solar Telescope of Hida Observatory. Hinode observed the emerging flux region with Ca II H and FeI Stokes IQUV filtergrams. In this study, detailed dynamics and the temporal evolution of the magnetic flux emergence was studied observationally. The event was first detected in the photospheric magnetic field signals; 3 minutes later, a horizontal expansion of the dark area was detected. Then, 7 minutes later than the horizontal expansion, the emerging loops were detected with a maximal rise speed of 2.1 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> at chromospheric heights. The observed dynamics of the emerging magnetic flux from the photosphere to the upper chromosphere was very consistent with the results of previous simulation studies. A gradual rising phase of flux tubes with a weak magnetic strength was confirmed by our observation.

articleTitle: Size Evolution of Early-Type Galaxies and Massive Compact Objects as Dark Matter
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The dramatic size evolution of early-type galaxies from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z\sim$</tex> 2 to 0 poses a new challenge in the theory of galaxy formation, which may not be explained by the standard picture. It is shown here that the size evolution can be explained if the non-baryonic cold dark matter is composed of compact objects having a mass scale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{5}M_\odot$</tex>. This form of dark matter is consistent with, or only weakly constrained by the currently available observations. The kinetic energy of the dark compact objects is transferred to stars by dynamical friction, and stars around the effective radius are pushed out to larger radii, resulting in a pure size evolution. This scenario has several good properties to explain the observations, including the ubiquitous nature of size evolution and faster disappearance of higher density galaxies.

articleTitle: Redshifts of Distant Blazars Limited by Fermi and VHE γ-Ray Observations
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Our goal is to limit the redshifts of three blazars, PG 1553+113, 3C 66A, and PKS 1424+240, through an investigation of their Fermi and VHE (very high energy) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray observations. We assume that the intrinsic spectra of PG 1553+113, 3C 66A, and PKS 1424+240 have no cutoff across the Fermi and VHE <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray energy ranges. The intrinsic spectra of VHE <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-rays are obtained through extrapolation of the Fermi spectra. Comparing the measured and intrinsic VHE spectra due to extragalactic background light (EBL) absorption, we give the redshift upper limits of three blazars, while assuming a specific EBL model. The redshift upper limits of PG 1553+113, 3C 66A, and PKS 1424+240 are 0.78, 0.58, and 1.19, respectively. Near to the TeV energy the optical depth of VHE <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> photons might be overestimated by the Franceschini EBL model (Franceschini et al. 2008, A&A, 487, 837), or the second emission component might be present in the VHE spectra and lead the intrinsic photon index to be harder than the Fermi ones.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observation of the Southeastern Rim of the Cygnus Loop
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: X-ray measured metal abundances of the rim of the Cygnus Loop are known to have two patterns. One, seen at narrow regions along the outermost edge, is 0.5-times the solar value, and the other, seen in the remainder of the rim, is 0.2-times the solar value. While the former is “normal”, as the ISM around the Cygnus Loop, the latter is unexpectedly depleted, and its origin has been puzzling. We have been tackling this issue by observing the rims with X-ray observatories. So far, the normal abundance was observed only at regions where no cloud-shock interactions are suggested. On the contrary, based on our recent Suzaku observations, we find the normal abundance at the southeastern rim where cloud-shock interactions are evident. The spatial variation of the abundance there is similar to that in other normal abundance rims: the normal abundance is present along the outermost edge (4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\prime$</tex> width regions), while the inner region shows strongly depleted abundances. This structure has been confirmed both by the plasma model fit and by the model-free fit. We noticed that the rim regions showing normal abundance correspond to those with a relatively weak radio intensity. Since the Cygnus Loop is believed to be the result of a cavity explosion, we discuss that the abundance distribution is due to the abundance difference between the cavity wall and its outside. The origin of the depleted abundance still remains an open question.

articleTitle: Orbital Period Study of the RS CVn-Type Binary WW Draconis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The orbital period variation of the RS CVn-type binary system WW Dra was studied based on all available times of light minima. We confirmed that the orbital period of the binary shows a cyclical change with a large amplitude of 0.2495 days. We discussed in detail the mechanisms that could explain the period change of the system, especially the light-travel time orbit of a tertiary component or magnetic activity cycle. Of these two mechanisms, we find that the latter is more plausible.

articleTitle: Method of the Particle-in-Cell Simulation for the Y-Point in the Pulsar Magnetosphere
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Recent observations in the X-ray and Gamma-ray suggest that the emission region of the pulsar magnetosphere can be multifold. In particular, the open-close boundary of the magnetic field, so-called the Y-point, can be a new candidate place where magnetic field energy converts into plasma heat and/or flow energy. Here, we present a new Particle-in-Cell code, which can be applied to the Y-point of the pulsar magnetosphere in axisymmetric geometry. The electromagnetic solver is used in two-dimensional grid points with cylindrical coordinates (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>), while the particle solver operates in three-dimensional Cartesian coordinates (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>), where the Buneman–Boris method is used. The particle motion is treated in special relativity. The inner boundary conditions are set up to generate rotation of the magnetosphere by use of the force-free semi-analytic solution given by Uzdensky (2003, ApJ, 598, 446). The code has been verified by dispersion relations of all wave modes in electron-positron plasmas. The initial test run is also presented to demonstrate the Y-shaped structure at the top of the dead zone on the light cylinder. We suggest that the structure is variable with quasi-periodicity with magnetic reconnection, and that plasma will be accelerated and/or heated. In a time-averaged point of view, the break up of the ideal-MHD (magneto-hydrodynamics) condition takes place in the vicinity of the Y-point.

articleTitle: Discovery of K-Shell Emission Lines of Neutral Atoms in the Galactic Center Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The K-shell emission line of neutral iron from the Galactic center (GC) region is one of the keys concerning the structure and activity of the GC. The origin is still an open question, but possibly due either to X-ray radiation or to electron bombarding to neutral atoms. To address this issue, we analyzed the Suzaku X-ray spectrum from the GC region of intense neutral iron line emission, and report on the discovery of K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> lines of neutral argon, calcium, chrome, and manganese atoms. The equivalent widths of these K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> lines indicate that the metal abundances in the GC region should be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>1.6 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>4 of the solar value, depending on the X-ray and electron origins, respectively. On the other hand, the metal abundances in the hot plasma in the GC region are found to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>1–2 solar. These results favor that the origin of the neutral K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> lines is due to X-ray irradiation.

articleTitle: A New System Noise Measuring Method Using a 2-Bit Analog-to-Digital Converter
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a new measuring method for the system noise temperature, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm sys}$</tex>, using a 2-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Statistics of the digitized signal in a four-level quantization gives us information about the bias voltage and the variance, which reflects the power of the input signal. A comparison of the variances in hot and sky circumstances yields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm sys}$</tex> without a power meter. We performed experimental tests using the Kagoshima 6 m radio telescope and a 2-bit ADC. The linearity in the power–variance relation was better than 99% within the dynamic range of 10 dB. Digitally measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm sys}$</tex> was in agreement with that of a conventional measurement with a power meter, although the temperatures differed by 1.8%, or less, for elevations of 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex>–88<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex>. No significant impact was found by the bias voltages within a range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>3.7% to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>12.8% with respect to the threshold voltage. The proposed method is available for existing interferometers that have a multilevel ADC, and release us from troubles caused by power meters.

articleTitle: X-Ray Studies of HESS J1809–193 with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Suzaku observed the region including HESS J1809-193, a TeV unidentified source, and confirmed the existence of extended hard X-ray emission previously reported by ASCA, as well as hard X-ray emission from PSR J1809-1917 in this region. A one-dimensional profile of the diffuse emission is represented along with a Gaussian model with a best-fit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> of 7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\prime \pm$</tex> 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\prime$</tex>. The diffuse emission extends for at least 21 pc (at the 3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> level, assuming a distance of 3.5 kpc), and has a hard spectrum with a photon index of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \sim$</tex> 1.7. The hard spectrum suggests a pulsar wind nebula origin, which is also strengthened by the hard X-ray emission from PSR J1809-1917, itself. Thanks to the low background of Suzaku XIS, we were able to investigate the spatial variation of the energy spectrum, but no systematic spectral change in the extended emission was found. These results imply that the X-ray emitting pulsar wind electrons can travel up to 21 pc from the pulsar without any noticeable energy loss via synchrotron emission.

articleTitle: DM Delphini: A Progenitor of a Contact Binary with a Compact Tertiary Companion
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The orbital period of the short-period eclipsing binary DM Del was analyzed by using two newly determined eclipse times together with the others compiled from the literature. It has been discovered that the period shows a long-time continuous decrease at a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dP/dt = -$</tex>2.27 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-7}$</tex> d yr<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, while it undergoes a cyclic variation with a period of 31.73 years. Meanwhile, photometric light curves of a close binary in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> bands, published by Güdür et al., were analyzed with the 2003 version of the W–D code. It was found that the system is a semi-detached binary with a lobe-filling primary and a mass ratio of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q =$</tex> 0.55. The long-time period decrease can be explained by mass transfer from the primary to the secondary. This is consistent with the semi-detached configuration. The geometrical structure of the binary and the long-term period decrease suggest that DM Del may be a progenitor of an overcontact binary or just in a broken-contact stage predicted by thermal relaxation oscillations. A cyclic period change reveals the presence of a tertiary unseen companion that may play an important role in the formation of the close binary by removing angular momentum from the central system.

articleTitle: Erratum: Chemical Abundances of the Outer Halo Stars in the Milky Way
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

articleTitle: Age-Determination Method of Pre-Main Sequence Stars with High-Resolution I-Band Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a new method for determining the age of late-K type pre-main sequence (PMS) stars by deriving their surface gravity from high-resolution I-band spectroscopy. Since PMS stars contract as they evolve, their age can be estimated by the surface gravity. We used the equivalent width ratio (EWR) of nearby absorption lines that are free of uncertainties due to veiling, to make a surface-gravity diagnostic of PMS stars. The ratios of Fe (8186.7 Å and 8204.9 Å) and Na (8183.3 Å and 8194.8 Å) absorption lines were calculated for giants, main-sequence stars, and weak-line T Tauri stars. The samples were nearly equal in effective temperature. The EWR of Fe and Na, Fe/Na, decreases significantly with increasing surface gravity, indicating that Fe/Na is a desirable diagnostic tool for deriving the surface gravity of PMS stars. The surface gravity of PMS stars with 0.8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ M_{\odot}$</tex> can be determined with accuracies of 0.1–0.2, which estimates the age of PMS stars within a factor of 1.5, on average.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Studies of Limb Spicules. I Radial and Turbulent Velocities
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We made high-resolution spectroscopic observations of limb spicules in H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> using the Vertical Spectrograph of Domeless Solar Telescope at Hida Observatory. While more than half of the observed spicules have Gaussian line-profiles, some spicules have distinctly asymmetric profiles, which can be fitted to two Gaussian components. The faster component has radial velocities of 10–40 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> and Doppler widths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>0.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\AA$</tex>, which suggest that it is from a single spicule oriented nearly along the line-of-sight. Profiles of the slower components and the single-Gaussian type show very similar characteristics. Their radial velocities are less than 10 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, and the Doppler widths are 0.6–0.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\AA$</tex>. Nonthermal “macroturbulent” velocities on the order of 30 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> are required so as to explain these width values.

articleTitle: MAXI GSC Observations of a Spectral State Transition in the Black Hole Candidate XTE J1752–223
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the first results on the black-hole candidate XTE J1752<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>223 from the Gas Slit Camera (GSC) aboard the Monitor of All-sky X-ray Image (MAXI) on the International Space Station. Including the onset of an outburst reported by the Proportional Counter Array aboard the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer on 2009 October 23, MAXI / GSC has been monitoring this source approximately 10 times per day with high sensitivity in the 2–20 keV band. XTE J1752<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>223 was initially in a low / hard state during the first 3 months. An anti-correlated behavior between the 2–4 keV and 4–20 keV bands was observed around 2010 January 20, indicating that the source exhibited a spectral transition to the high / soft state. A transient radio jet may have been ejected when the source was in the intermediate state where the spectrum was roughly explained by a power-law with a photon index of 2.5–3.0. The unusually long period in the initial low / hard state implies a slow variation in the mass-accretion rate, and a dramatic soft X-ray increase may be explained by a sudden appearance of the accretion disk component with a relatively low innermost temperature (0.4–0.7 keV). Such a low temperature might suggest that the maximum accretion rate was just above the critical gas-evaporation rate required for the state transition.

articleTitle: Early Spectroscopy of the 2010 Outburst of U Scorpii
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present early spectroscopy of the recurrent nova U Sco during an outburst in 2010. We successfully obtained time-series spectra during the period of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\rm d} =$</tex> 0.37–0.44 d, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\rm d}$</tex> is the time that elapsed since the discovery of the present outburst. This is the first time-resolved spectroscopy on the first night of U Sco outbursts. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\rm d} \sim$</tex> 0.4 d, the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line consists of a blue-shifted (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>5000 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) narrow absorption component and a wide, triple-peak emission one: blue (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim-$</tex>3000 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>), central (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>), and red (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim+$</tex>3000 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) peaks. The blue and red peaks developed more rapidly than the central one for the first night. This rapid variation would be caused by the growth of aspherical wind produced during the earliest stage of the outburst. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\rm d} =$</tex> 1.4 d, the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line has a nearly flat-topped profile with weak blue and red peaks at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim \pm$</tex>3000 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>. This profile can be attributed to a nearly spherical shell, while the asphericity growing on the first night still remains. The wind asphericity is less significant after <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\rm d} =$</tex> 9 d.

articleTitle: Optical Spectroscopy of Candidates of Young Stellar Objects in NGC 1333
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out low-resolution optical spectroscopy of 14 low-luminosity young stellar object (YSO) candidates in the NGC 1333 cluster. These objects were previously identified by a near-infrared imaging survey. Eleven objects were confirmed to be YSOs by the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line emission. The strengths of the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission are correlated with the near-infrared excesses of the objects. The spectral types of all YSOs are estimated to be M-type, indicative of low mass. Comparisons of the results of our spectroscopic observations and previous photometric observations with evolutionary tracks on the HR diagram suggest two objects to be young brown dwarfs.

articleTitle: Millimeter Light Curve with Abrupt Jump in Cyg X-3 2008 April–May Outburst
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Cyg X-3 is a well-known microquasar with a bipolar relativistic jet. Its famous giant radio outbursts have been repeated once every several years. However, the behavior of the millimeter-wave emission has remained unclear because of limitations of time resolution in previous observations. We report here on millimeter wave observations of Cyg X-3 experiencing giant outbursts with one of the finest time resolutions. We have found a series of short-lived flares with amplitudes of 1–2 Jy in the millimeter light curve of the 2008 April–May outburst. They have flat spectra at around 100 GHz. We have also found abrupt and large amplitude flux density changes with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex>-folding time of 3.6 min or less. The source size of Cyg X-3 is constrained to within 0.4 AU, and the brightness temperature is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_\mathrm{B}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>rsim$</tex> 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{11}\ $</tex>K.

articleTitle: Study of the Large-Scale Temperature Structure of the Perseus Cluster with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on a study of the large-scale temperature structure of the Perseus cluster with Suzaku, using observational data of four pointings of the 30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime}$</tex> offset regions, together with data from the central region. Thanks to the Hard X-ray Detector (HXD-PIN: 10–60 keV), Suzaku can determine the temperature of hot galaxy clusters. We performed a spectral analysis by considering the temperature structure and the collimator response of the PIN correctly. As a result, we found that the upper limit of the temperature in the outer region is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>14 keV, and an extremely hot gas, which was reported for RX J1347.5-1145 and Abell 3667, was not found in the Perseus cluster. This indicates that the Perseus cluster has not recently experienced a major merger.

articleTitle: A Binary Shaped Mask Coronagraph for a Segmented Pupil
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the concept of a binary shaped mask coronagraph applicable to a telescope pupil including obscuration, based on previous work on a binary shaped pupil mask by Kasdin et al. (2005, Appl. Opt., 44, 1117) and Vanderbei (1999, Optimization methods and software, 11, 451). Solutions with multi-barcode masks that “skip over” the obscuration are shown for various types of pupils of the telescope, such as SUBARU, JWST, SPICA, and other examples. The number of diffraction tails in the point-spread function of the coronagraphic image is reduced to two, thus offering a large discovery angle. The concept of mask rotation is also presented, which allows a post-processing removal of diffraction tails, and provides a 360<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex> continuous discovery angle. It is suggested that the presented concept offers solutions that potentially will allow large telescopes with a segmented pupil in the future to be used as platforms for coronagraphs.

articleTitle: A Period Investigation of the δ Scuti Star AN Lyncis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present 9 new times of light maximum of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta$</tex> Scuti star AN Lyncis based on photometric observations from the years 2008–2010. Together with 194 times of the light maximum from the literature, a detailed study of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex> diagram with data spanning over three decades has led to a new ephemeris formula. A cyclic change in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex> diagram is also suggested by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex> method, where the cyclic period is about 17.7 yr. With the available data, we have found that the Fourier amplitude of AN Lyncis is changing in sync with a change of the pulsation period. Simple arguments are given for a possible mechanism affecting the cyclic change.

articleTitle: A New Candidate of a Cluster of Galaxies, 2XMM J045637.2+522411
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present XMM-Newton and Suzaku results of an X-ray source, 2XMM J045637.2+522411, found during an observation of a galactic supernova remnant (SNR), G156.2+5.7. By comparing its radial profile with the point-spread function, we found that 2XMM J045637.2+522411 is an extended source. X-ray spectra exhibited a line-like structure at 5.7–5.8 keV. Since no abundant element emits an X-ray line at 5–6 keV in the rest-frame, and the most intense emission line in the 5–7 keV energy band is a Fe-K line, the line is likely to be a redshifted Fe-K line. The overall spectra can be represented by a thin-thermal plasma model with a temperature of 3–4 keV and a redshift of 0.15–0.17. No intensity variation was found in the light curve. The observational results indicate that 2XMM J045637.2+522411 is likely to be a cluster of galaxies.

articleTitle: Revisit to the Nuclear Spin Temperature of NH$_{3}$ in Comet C/2001 Q4 (NEAT) Based on High-Dispersion Spectra of Cometary NH$_{2}$
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Ortho-to-Para abundance ratio (OPR) of cometary molecules is considered to be one of primordial characters of comeary ices, which has information concerning their formation. In order to determine the OPR of cometary ammonia (NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{3}$</tex>), high-dispersion spectra in the optical wavelength region have been the most powerful tool, since NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> is a photo-dissociation product of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{3}$</tex>, and NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> has a strong electronic transition in the optical region. Here we present an improved procedure to derive the OPR of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> (OPR of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{3}$</tex> is derived from that of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>) from the high-dispersion spectra of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> in comets. We consider (1) the contamination of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> lines by the C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> Swan-band lines, (2) the influence by the telluric absorption lines, and (3) multiple measurements of OPR from different vibronic bands of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> in the optical region, to achieve a more accurate determination of OPRs than that in previous studies. We applied the new method to the spectrum of comet C/2001 Q4 (NEAT) for which the OPR of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> was determined in the previous study. The derived OPR of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> is 3.23<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \pm $</tex>0.03, and this is more accurate than before. The OPR of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{3}$</tex> is estimated to be 1.12<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \pm $</tex>0.02, which corresponds to a nuclear spin temperature (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_\mathrm{spin}$</tex>) of 30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+2}_{-1} $</tex>K. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_\mathrm{spin}$</tex> value of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{3}$</tex> is basically consistent with the temperature inferred from the mixing ratio of CO with respect to H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>O found in the same comet.

articleTitle: On the Light-Bending Model of X-Ray Variability of MCG –6–30–15
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have applied the light-bending model of X-ray variability to Suzaku data of the Seyfert 1 galaxy MCG <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>6–30–15. We analyzed the energy dependence of the root mean square variability, and discussed conditions necessary for the model to explain the characteristic decrease of the source variability at around 5–8 keV. A model, where the X-ray source moves radially rather than vertically close to the disk surface, can indeed reproduce the reduced variability near the energy of the Fe K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha}$</tex> line, although the formal fit quality is poor. The model then predicts the energy spectra, which can be compared to observational data. The spectra are strongly reflection dominated, and do not provide a good fit to Suzaku spectral data of the source. The inconsistency of this result with some previous claims can be traced to our using data in a broader energy band, where the effects of a warm absorber in the spectrum cannot be neglected.

articleTitle: Evolution of the Kippenhahn–Schlüter Prominence Model Magnetic Field under Cowling Resistivity
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the results from 1.5D diffusion simulations of the Kippenhahn–Schlüter prominence model magnetic field evolution under the influence of the ambipolar terms of Cowling resistivity. We show that initially the evolution is determined by the ratio of the horizontal and vertical magnetic fields, which gives current sheet thinning (thickening) when this ratio is small (large) and a marginal case where a new characteristic current sheet length scale is formed. After a timespan greater than the Cowling resistivity time, the current sheet thickens as a power law of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> independent of the ratio of the field strengths. These results imply that when Cowling resistivity is included in the model, the tearing instability time scale is reduced by more than one order of magnitude when the ratio of the horizontal field to the vertical field is 20% or less. These results imply that, over the course of its lifetime, the structure of the prominence can be significantly altered by Cowling resistivity, and in some cases will allow the tearing instability to occur.

articleTitle: Proper Motions with Subaru II. A Sample in the Subaru/XMM-Newton Deep Survey Field
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We search for stars with proper motions in a set of deep Subaru images, covering about 0.48 square degrees to a depth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i^{\prime} \simeq$</tex> 26, taken over a span of five and a half years. We follow the methods described in Richmond et al. (2009, PASJ, 61, 97) to reduce and analyze this dataset. We present a sample of 69 stars with motions of high significance, and discuss briefly the populations from which they are likely drawn. Based on photometry and motions alone, we expect that 14 of the candidates may be white dwarfs. Our candidate with the largest proper motion is surprisingly faint and likely to prove interesting: its colors and motions suggest that it might be an M dwarf moving at over 500 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> or an L dwarf in the halo.

articleTitle: A Search for Water Masers in the Saturnian System
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have searched for H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>O 6(1,6)–5(2,3) maser emission at 22.235 GHz from several Saturnian satellites with the Nobeyama 45 m radio telescope in 2009 May. Objects of our observation are Titan, Hyperion, Enceladus, and Atlas, from which Pogrebenko et al. (2009, A&A, 494, L1) reported having detected water masers at 22.235 GHz, and in addition are Iapetus and other inner satellites. We detected no emission of the water-maser line from all of the satellites observed, although the sensitivities of our observation are comparable to, or even better than, those of Pogrebenko et al. (2009, A&A, 494, L1). We infer from our observation that the water-maser emission from the Saturnian system is extremely weak, or sporadic in itself. Both monitoring over a long period and obtaining statistical results are important for gaining a further understanding of the water-maser emission in the Saturnian system.

Author Keywords: planets and satellites: individual (Titan, Hyperion, Iapetus, Enceladus, Atlas)
planets and satellites: individual (Titan, Hyperion, Iapetus, Enceladus, Atlas)

articleTitle: Chemical Variation in Molecular Cloud Cores in the Orion A Cloud
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have observed molecular cloud cores in the Orion A giant molecular cloud (GMC) in CCS, HC<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>N, DNC, and HN<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>C to study their chemical characteristics. We detected CCS in the Orion A GMC for the first time. CCS was detected in about a third of the observed cores. The cores detected in CCS are not localized, but widely distributed over the Orion A GMC. The CCS peak intensity of the core tends to be high in the southern region of the Orion A GMC. The HC<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>N peak intensity of the core also tends to be high in the southern region, while there are HC<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>N intense cores near Orion KL, which is not seen in CCS. The core associated with Orion KL shows a broad HC<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>N line profile, and the star-formation activity near to Orion KL seems to enhance the HC<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>N emission. The column density ratio of NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> to CCS is lower near the middle of the filament, and higher toward the northern and southern regions along the Orion A GMC filament. This ratio is known to trace the chemical evolution in nearby dark cloud cores, but seems to be affected by the core gas temperature in the Orion A GMC: cores with low NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> to CCS column density ratios tend to have a warmer gas temperature. The value of the column density ratio of DNC to HN<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>C is generally similar to that in dark cloud cores, but becomes lower around Orion KL due to a higher gas temperature.

Author Keywords: ISM: individual (Orion Nebula, Orion Molecular Cloud)

articleTitle: Water Production Rate of the Jupiter-Family Comet 46P/Wirtanen in the 2008 Apparition with the Subaru Telescope/IRCS
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the water production rate of comet 46P/Wirtanen in its 2008 apparition, determined from high-dispersion near-infrared spectroscopic observations. Comet 46P/Wirtanen, one of Jupiter-family comets, was the target of the ROSETTA mission in the past. Observations of comet 46P were carried out in the middle of 2008 February with the Subaru telescope and Infrared Camera and Spectrograph (IRCS) instrument. We detected three water emission lines, and the water production rate was determined to be (1.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.2) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{28}\ $</tex>molecules s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> on 2008 February 19 near the perihelion passage of the comet. This was the first direct detection of water in the coma of comet 46P. We compared our result with the water production rate determined from radio observations near the perihelion passage in the same apparition, and we found that the rate of radio observations is consistent with our value within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \sigma$</tex> errors. We also compared the water production rates observed in the 2008 apparition with other results observed in the 1997 apparition. We found that the water production rates in 2008 are consistent with those in 1997. There was no secular change of water production rates around its perihelion passage in recent decades for comet 46P.

articleTitle: Discovery of Multiple High-Velocity Narrow Circumstellar NaI D Lines in Nova V1280 Sco
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We discovered multiple high-velocity (ranging from -900 to -650 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) and narrow (FWHM <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 15 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) absorption components corresponding to both the D2 and the D1 lines of Na I on a high-dispersion spectrum of V1280 Sco, observed on 2009 May 9 (UT), 814 d after the V band maximum. Subsequent observations carried out on 2009 June and July confirmed at least 11 distinct absorption components in both systems. Some components had deepened during the two-month period while their HWHMs and wavelengths remained nearly constant. We suggest that these high-velocity components originated in cool clumpy gas clouds moving on the line-of-sight, produced during interactions between pre-existing cool circumstellar gas and high-velocity gas ejected in the nova explosion. The optical region spectrum of V1280 Sco in 2009 is dominated by the continuum radiation, and exhibits no forbidden line characterizing the nebular phase of typical novae. Permitted Fe II lines show doubly peaked emission profiles, and some strong Fe II lines are accompanied by a blue-shifted (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim -$</tex> 255 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) absorption component. However, no high-velocity and narrow components corresponding to those of Na I could be detected in Fe II lines nor in the Balmer lines. The 255 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> low-velocity absorption component most probably originates in the wind from the nova.

articleTitle: A Multicolour Photometric Study for the W Ursae Majoris Type Binary LR Camelopardalis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A CCD multicolour photometry for the eclipsing binary LR Camelopardalis, obtained on 2008 December 19 and 2010 January 29 and 30 at the Xinglong Station of NAOC, is presented. Using the Wilson–Devinney binary code, a photometric solution was simultaneously derived from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BVR$</tex> light curves. The results show that LR Cam belongs to a W-type contact binary, with a mass ratio of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q =$</tex> 0.300(1) and an overcontact degree of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f =$</tex> 23.5(5)%, indicating that LR Cam is a weak-contact binary. The asymmetric light curves (i.e., the O’Connell effect) were modeled by a dark spot on the more massive component. From the (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex>) curve of LR Cam, it is found that the orbital period shows a sine-like variation superimposed on a secular period increase. The quasi-sinusoidal variation, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A =$</tex> 0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\rm d}\!\!\!.$</tex>0039(1), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{3} =$</tex> 5.34(2) yr, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^\prime =$</tex> 0.56(3), may more likely result from a light-time effect via the presence of a third body. The long-term period increases at a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dP/dt = +$</tex>0.65(9) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-7}\ $</tex>d yr<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, which may be interpreted by mass transfer from the less-massive component to the more-massive one. With mass transferring, LR Cam may evolve into a broken-contact binary.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of the Mergers of Black Hole–Neutron Star Binaries
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Black hole (BH)–neutron star (NS) mergers have been studied as one of the primary sources of gravitational wave radiation and a strong candidate for the sources of short-hard gamma-ray bursts (SHBs). In this work, we investigated the criterion for a tidal disruption to occur outside the innermost stable circular orbit with various initial conditions of BH and NS. We studied the merger processes due to Roche-lobe overflow by an analytical method with Newtonian orbital functions. By using the polytropic equation of state for the NS, we calculated the time scale of merger for both irrotating (IR) and corotationg (CR) configurations. The resulting time scale is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3} $</tex>s for the IR case, which agrees well with that of hydrodynamic simulations. We present a simple comparison with the most recent simulation result. The connection to the SHBs is also discussed.

articleTitle: Forecast for Phoenicids in 2008, 2014, and 2019
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report here on a complete forecast of the activity of future Phoenicid meteor showers in the period 2008–2020. We detail predictions of Phoenicids activities during three years: 2008, 2014, and 2019. In 2008, the trail of 1866 will intersect with the Earth orbit. In 2014, the origin of the activity will be due to several trails formed from the 19th to the early 20th centuries. The display in 2014 will be the most spectacular meteor showers among the three cases because of a favorable geometric condition. In 2019, the Earth will approach four trails formed between 1872 and 1882, and one trail of 1946. Since the parent body had not been observed during the above-mentioned period, the activity of these meteor showers is important for estimating the degree of cometary activity for this parent body during this period.

articleTitle: Optical and Near-Infrared Photometry of Nova V2362 Cyg: Rebrightening Event and Dust Formation
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present optical and near-infrared (NIR) photometry of a classical nova, V2362 Cyg (= Nova Cygni 2006). V2362 Cyg experienced a peculiar rebrightening during the period between 100 and 240 d after the maximum of the nova. Our multicolor observation indicates the emergence of a pseudophotosphere with an effective temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>9000 K at the rebrightening maximum. After the rebrightening maximum, the object showed a slow fading homogeneously in all of the used bands for one week. This implies that the fading soon after the rebrightening maximum (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim\ $</tex>1 week) was caused by a slowly shrinking pseudophotosphere. Then, the NIR flux drastically increased, while the optical flux steeply declined. The optical and NIR fluxes were consistent with blackbody radiation with a temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>1500 K during this NIR rising phase. These facts are likely to be explained by dust formation in the nova ejecta. Assuming an optically thin case, we estimated the dust mass to be 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-10}$</tex>–10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-8}\ M_{\odot}$</tex>, which is less than those in typical dust-forming novae. These results support the senario that a second, long-lasting outflow which caused the rebrightening interacted with a fraction of the initial outflow and formed dust grains.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observations of the Supernova Remnant N23 in the Large Magellanic Cloud
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: X-ray emission from the supernova remnant N23 in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) has been studied using the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) onboard Suzaku. Thanks to a superior energy resolution of the XIS in the soft X-ray band, we resolved H-like and He-like Oxygen K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission lines from N23 with unprecedentedly high quality, and as a result, identified a new optically thin thermal emission component with a temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>0.2 keV, as well as that with a temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>0.5–0.7 keV, previously known. This alters the estimate of the ionization timescale, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_{\rm e}t$</tex>, from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{10-11}\ $</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}\ $</tex>s to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>rsim\ $</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}\ $</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}\ $</tex>s. Under the assumption that N23 is still in the Sedov phase, its age, evaluated from the newly discovered low-temperature component, is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>8000 yr, although it is possible that N23 has already moved into the radiative phase. The abundances of the heavy elements are found to be roughly consistent with those of the LMC average, which indicates that the origin of the X-ray emission of N23 is swept-up ambient material, as expected from its ionization timescale.

articleTitle: Detection of a Cyclic Period Change in the W UMa-Type System HT Virginis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: HT Vir is a well-known quadruple system with three components visible in the spectra. However, the cyclic variation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O - C$</tex> diagram has not been presented until now. To search for a variation in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O - C$</tex> diagram of HT Vir, we monitored it from 2007 March to 2009 February, and as a result, 7 times of light minimum were obtained. Also, 3 times of light minimum were determined by us with photoelectric data obtained at Mt. Suhora observatory by using three channel photometers attached on the 60-cm Cassegrain telescope (Zola et al. 2005). Based on 56 times of light minimum, we report the discovery of a cyclic variation in the orbital period of HT Vir. It was found that the orbital period of the binary shows a 30.5 yr cyclic change with a semiamplitude of 0.0066 d. The period variation may be caused by a disturbance of component A to the contact system orbit. More times of light minimum with high precision are needed to check the nature of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O - C$</tex> plot in the future.

articleTitle: AKARI Infrared Observations of the Edge-On Spiral Galaxy NGC 3079
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present AKARI near- to far-infrared images of the nearby edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 3079 in 10 photometric bands. The spectral energy distribution consists of continuum emission from dust with a single temperature of 28–33 K together with strong mid-infrared emission features from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). We derived dust masses of 5.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{6}\ M$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{\odot}$</tex> and 1.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^7\ M$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{\odot}$</tex> for the central 4 kpc region and the whole galaxy, respectively, and found that the gas-to-dust mass ratio is unusually high in the central region (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>1100), and even for the whole galaxy (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>860). The ratio of the surface brightness distribution at a wavelength of 7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \mu$</tex>m to that at 11<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \mu$</tex>m suggests that the properties of PAHs have spatial variations. The emission from ionized and neutral PAHs is relatively strong in the center and the disk regions, respectively, suggesting a stronger radiation field, and thus relatively active star formation in the center. Yet, the total infrared luminosities of the galaxy indicate rather low star formation rates. These results suggest that NGC 3079 is in an early-phase starburst stage.

articleTitle: Broad Balmer-Line Absorption in SDSS J172341.10+555340.5
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the discovery of Balmer-line absorption from H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> to H9 in an iron low-ionizaton broad absorption line (FeLoBAL) quasar, SDSS J172341.10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>555340.5, by near-infrared spectroscopy with the Cooled Infrared Spectrograph and Camera for OHS (CISCO) attached to the Subaru Telescope. The redshift of the Balmer-line absorption troughs is 2.0530<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.0003, and it is blueshifted by 5370 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> from the Balmer emission lines. It is more than 4000 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> blueshifted from the previously known UV absorption lines. We detected relatively strong (EW<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{\rm rest} =$</tex> 20 Å) [O III] emission lines that are similar to those found in other broad absorption line quasars with Balmer-line absorption. We also derived the column density of neutral hydrogen of 5.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{17}\ $</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex> by using the curve of growth and taking account of Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> trapping. We searched for UV absorption lines that had the same redshift with Balmer-line absorption, and found Al III and Fe III absorption lines at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z =$</tex> 2.053 that correspond to previously unidentified absorption lines, and the presence of other blended troughs that were difficult to identify.

articleTitle: Optical Light Curves of Luminous Eclipsing Black Hole X-Ray Binaries
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We examined optical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>-band light curves in luminous eclipsing black hole X-ray binaries, using a supercritical accretion/outflow model that is more realistic than the formerly used ones. In order to compute the theoretical light curve in the binary system, we did not only apply the global analytic solution of the disk, but also included the effect of optically thick outflow. We found that the depth of eclipse of the companion star by the disk changed dramatically when including the effect of the outflow. Due to the effect of outflow, we could reproduce the optical light curve for typical binary parameters in SS 433. Our model with an outflow velocity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v \sim$</tex> 3000 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> could fit the whole shape of the averaged <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>-band light curve in SS 433, but we found a possible parameter range consistent with observations, such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{M} \sim$</tex> 5000–10000<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ L_{\rm E}/c^2$</tex> (with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm E}$</tex> being the Eddington luminosity and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> being the speed of light) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm C} =$</tex> 10000<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ > $</tex>K–14000 K for the accretion rate and donor star temperature, respectively. Furthermore, we briefly discuss observational implications for ultraluminous X-ray sources.

articleTitle: Orbital Period Change of the Eclipsing Binary System SZ Piscium
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We collected and tabulated all available times of the light minimum of the eclipsing RS CVn-type binary system SZ Psc that we could find in the literature. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex> curve was constructed by means of a weighted least-squares method. It was found that a sinusoidal variation, with a period of 55.5 yr and an amplitude of 0.<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\rm d}$</tex>2667, is superimposed on a long-term period decrease at a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dP/dt = -$</tex>(2.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm $</tex>0.2) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-8} $</tex>days/day. Since one component of SZ Psc is a late-type star, which shows strong Ca II H & K emission lines, the orbital period variation may be caused by the magnetic activity of the system.

articleTitle: Spicule Dynamics over a Plage Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We studied spicular jets over a plage area and derived their dynamic characteristics using Hinode Solar Optical Telescope (SOT) high-resolution images. A target plage region was near to the west limb of the solar disk. This location permitted us to study the dynamics of spicular jets without any overlapping effect of spicular structures along the line of sight. In this work, to increase the ease with which we could identify spicules on the disk, we applied the image processing method ‘MadMax’ developed by Koutchmy et al. (1989). It enhances fine, slender structures (like jets), over a diffuse background. We identified 169 spicules over the target plage. This sample permited us to derive statistically reliable results regarding spicular dynamics. The properties of plage spicules can be summarized as follows: (1) In a plage area, we clearly identified spicular jet features. (2) They were shorter in length than the quiet region limb spicules, and followed a ballistic motion under constant deceleration. (3) The majority (80%) of the plage spicules showed a cycle of rise and retreat, while 10% of them faded out without a complete retreat phase. (4) The deceleration of the spicule was proportional to the velocity of ejection (i.e., the initial velocity).

articleTitle: Explosion Geometry of a Rotating 13 $\ M_{\odot}$ Star Driven by the SASI-Aided Neutrino-Heating Supernova Mechanism
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: By performing axisymmetric hydrodynamic simulations of core-collapse supernovae with spectral neutrino transport based on the isotropic diffusion source approximation scheme, we support the assumption that the neutrino-heating mechanism aided by the standing accretion shock instability (SASI) and convection can initiate an explosion of a 13<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ M_{\odot}$</tex> star. Our results show that bipolar explosions are more likely to be associated with models that include rotation. We point out that models that form a north–south symmetric bipolar explosion can lead to larger explosion energies than the corresponding unipolar explosions can.

articleTitle: The Rossiter–McLaughlin Effect of the Transiting Exoplanet XO-4b
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report photometric and radial velocity observations of the XO-4 transiting planetary system, conducted with the FLWO 1.2 m telescope and the 8.2 m Subaru Telescope. Based on the new light curves, the refined transit ephemeris of XO-4b is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 4.1250828<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.0000040 d and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm c}$</tex> [BJD<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{\rm TDB}$</tex>] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 2454485.93323<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.00039. We measured the Rossiter–McLaughlin effect of XO-4b and estimated the sky-projected angle between the stellar spin axis and the planetary orbital axis to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>46<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ\!\!\!.$</tex>7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ ^{{+8^\circ\!\!\!.1}}_{{-6^\circ\!\!\!.1}}$</tex>. This measurement of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> is less robust than in some other cases because the impact parameter of the transit is small, causing a strong degeneracy between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> and the projected stellar rotational velocity. Nevertheless, our finding of a spin–orbit misalignment suggests that the migration process for XO-4b involved few-body dynamics rather than interaction with a gaseous disk. In addition, our result conforms with the pattern reported by Winn et al. (2010, ApJ, 718, L145) that high obliquities are preferentially found for stars with effective temperatures hotter than 6250 K.

articleTitle: Identification of CXOU J171405.7−381031 as a New Magnetar with XMM-Newton
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed the 3.8 s pulsar CXOU J171405.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>381031 with XMM-Newton, and discovered a significant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot P$</tex> of 6.40<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.05 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-11}\ $</tex>s s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> from this source for the first time, with the aid of archival Chandra data. The characteristic age (950 yr), the magnetic field strength (5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{14}\ $</tex>G), and the spin-down luminosity (4.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{34}\ $</tex>erg s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) derived from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot P$</tex> lead us to conclude that CXOU J171405.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>381031 should be identified as a new magnetar. The obtained characteristic age indicates that CXOU J171405.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>381031 is the youngest among all known anomalous X-ray pulsars, and is consistent with the age estimated from the thermal X-rays of the associated supernova remnant. The ratio between the 2–10 keV luminosity and the spin-down luminosity is almost unity, which implies that CXOU J171405.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>381031 is the key source to connect magnetars with traditional radio pulsars.

articleTitle: On the Relation between Surge Activities and a Photospheric Horizontal Velocity Field
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
