These values correspond to a chance probability of 2.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-35}$</tex> and 4.27 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-31}$</tex>, respectively. It is a very important issue whether these tight correlations are an intrinsic property of GRBs, or are caused by some selection effect of observations. In this paper, we examine how the truncation of the detector sensitivity affects the correlations, and conclude they are surely intrinsic properties of GRBs. Next we investigate origins of the dispersion of the correlations by studying their brightness and redshift dependence. Here, the brightness (flux or fluence) dependence would be regarded as being an estimator of the bias due to the detector threshold. We found a weak fluence-dependence in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\rm p}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\rm iso}$</tex> correlations and a redshift dependence in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\rm p}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm p}$</tex> correlation both at the 2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \sigma$</tex> statistical level. These two effects may contribute to the dispersion of the correlations, which is larger than the statistical uncertainty. We discuss a possible reason of these dependences and give a future prospect to improve the correlations.

articleTitle: Suzaku Constraints on Soft and Hard Excess Emissions from Abell 2199
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The nearby (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z =$</tex> 0.03015) cluster of galaxies Abell 2199 was observed by Suzaku in X-rays, with five pointings for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 20 ks each. From the XIS data, the temperature and metal abundance profiles were derived out to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 700 kpc (0.4 times the virial radius). Both of these quantities decrease gradually from the center to peripheries by a factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 2, while the oxygen abundance tends to be flat. The temperature within 12<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^\prime$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 430 kpc) is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 4 keV, and the 0.5–10 keV X-ray luminosity integrated up to 30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^\prime$</tex> is (2.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.1) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{44}$</tex>erg s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, in agreement with previous XMM-Newton measurements. Above this thermal emission, no significant excess was found either in the XIS range below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 1 keV, or in the HXD-PIN range above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 15 keV. The 90%-confidence upper limit on the emission measure of an assumed 0.2 keV warm gas is (3.7–7.5) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{62}$</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}$</tex>arcmin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex>, which is 3.7–7.6 times tighter than the detection reported with XMM-Newton. The 90%-confidence upper limit on the 20–80 keV luminosity of any power-law component is 1.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{43}$</tex>erg s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, assuming a photon index of 2.0. Although this upper limit does not reject the possible 2.1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> detection by the BeppoSAX PDS, it is a factor of 2.1 tighter than that of the PDS if both are considered upper limits. The non-detection of the hard excess can be reconciled with the upper limit on diffuse radio emission, without invoking very low magnetic fields (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> 0.073<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>G) which were suggested previously.

articleTitle: Survey of Period Variations of Superhumps in SU UMa-Type Dwarf Novae. II The Second Year (2009–2010)
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Continued from Kato et al. (2009, PASJ, 61, S395), we collected the times of superhump maxima for 68 SU UMa-type dwarf novae, mainly observed during the 2009–2010 season. The newly obtained data confirmed the basic findings reported in Kato et al. (ibid.): the presence of stages A–C and the predominance of positive period derivatives during stage B in systems with superhump periods shorter than 0.07 d. There was a systematic difference in the period derivatives for the systems with superhump periods longer than 0.075 d between this study and Kato et al. (ibid.). We suggest that this difference was possibly caused by a relative lack of frequently outbursting SU UMa-type dwarf novae in this period regime in the present study. We recorded a strong beat phenomenon during the 2009 superoutburst of IY UMa. A close correlation between the beat period and the superhump period suggests that the changing angular velocity of the apsidal motion of the elliptical disk is responsible for the variation of the superhump periods. We also described three new WZ Sge-type objects with established early superhumps and one with likely early superhumps. We suggest that two systems, VX For and EL UMa, are WZ Sge-type dwarf novae with multiple rebrightenings. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex> variation in OT J213806.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>261957 suggests that the frequent absence of rebrightenings in very short-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\rm orb}$</tex> objects can be the result of a sustained superoutburst plateau at the epoch when usual SU UMa-type dwarf novae return to quiescence, preceding a rebrightening. We also present a formulation for a variety of Bayesian extensions to traditional period analyses.

articleTitle: Substellar Companions to Evolved Intermediate-Mass Stars: HD 145457 and HD 180314
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the detection of two substellar companions orbiting around evolved intermediate-mass stars by precise Doppler measurements at Subaru Telescope and Okayama Astrophysical Observatory. HD 145457 is a K0 giant with a mass of 1.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ M_{\odot}$</tex>, and has a planet of minimum mass, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2$</tex> sin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i =$</tex> 2.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ M_{\rm J}$</tex>, orbiting with a period of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P=176$</tex> d and eccentricity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e=0.11$</tex>. HD 180314 is also a K0 giant with 2.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ M_{\odot}$</tex>, and hosts a substellar companion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2$</tex> sin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i =$</tex> 22<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ M_{\rm J}$</tex>, which falls in the brown-dwarf mass regime, in an orbit with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P =$</tex> 396 d and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e =$</tex> 0.26. HD 145457 b is one of the innermost planets and HD 180314 b is the seventh candidate of a brown-dwarf-mass companion found around evolved intermediate-mass stars.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Simulations of Merging Galaxy Clusters: Non-Equilibrium Ionization State and Two-Temperature Structure
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigate a non-equilibrium ionization state and an electron–ion two-temperature structure of the intracluster medium (ICM) in merging galaxy clusters using a series of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body and hydrodynamic simulations. Mergers with various sets of mass ratios and impact parameters are systematically investigated, and it is found that, in most cases, ICM significantly departs from the ionization equilibrium state at the shock layers with a Mach number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>1.5–2.0 in the outskirts of the clusters, and the shock layers with a Mach number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>2–4 in front of the ICM cores. Accordingly, the intensity ratio between FeXXV and FeXXVI K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line emissions is significantly altered from that in the ionization equilibrium state. If the effect of the two-temperature structure of ICM is incorporated, the electron temperature is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>10%–20% and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>30%–50% lower than the mean temperature of ICM at the shock layers in the outskirts and in front of the ICM cores, respectively, and the deviation from the ionization equilibrium state becomes larger. We also address the dependence of the intensity ratio on the viewing angle with respect to the merging plane.

articleTitle: Dense and Warm Molecular Gas and Warm Dust in Nearby Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We performed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO (1–0), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (1–0), and HCN (1–0) single-dish observations (beam size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>14–18) toward nearby starburst and non-starburst galaxies using the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (1–0) and HCN (1–0) emissions were detected from all seven starburst galaxies, with the intensities of both lines being similar (i.e., the ratios are around unity). On the other hand, for the case of non-starburst galaxies, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (1–0) emission was detected from all three galaxies, while HCN (1–0) emission was weak, or not detected in past observations. This result indicates that the HCN<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$/{}^{13}$</tex>CO intensity ratios are significantly larger (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>1.15<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \pm $</tex>0.32) in the starburst galaxy samples than the non-starburst galaxy samples (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> 0.31<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \pm $</tex>0.14). The large-velocity-gradient model suggests that the molecular gas in the starburst galaxies has warmer and denser conditions than that in the non-starburst galaxies, and the photon-dominated-region model suggests that denser molecular gas is irradiated by a stronger interstellar radiation field in starburst galaxies than that in non-starburst galaxies. In addition, HCN<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$/{}^{13}$</tex>CO ratios in our sample galaxies exhibit strong correlations with the IRAS 25<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mu$</tex>m flux ratios. It is a well-established fact that there exists a strong correlation between dense molecular gas and star-formation activities, but our results suggest that the molecular gas temperature is also an important parameter.

articleTitle: Mass Function of Binary Massive Black Holes in Active Galactic Nuclei
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: If the activity of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is predominantly induced by major galaxy mergers, then a significant fraction of AGNs should harbor binary massive black holes in their centers. We have studied the mass function of binary massive black holes in nearby AGNs based on the observed AGN black-hole mass function and the theory of evolution of binary massive black holes interacting with a massive circumbinary disk within the framework of the coevolution of massive black holes and their host galaxies. The circumbinary disk is assumed to be steady, axisymmetric, geometrically thin, self-regulated, self-gravitating but nonfragmenting with a fixed fraction of the Eddington accretion rate, which is typically one tenth of the Eddington value. The timescale of orbital decay is then estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{8}\ $</tex>yr for equal mass black holes, being independent of the black-hole mass, semimajor axis, and viscosity parameter, but dependent on the black-hole mass ratio, Eddington ratio, and mass-to-energy conversion efficiency. This makes it possible for any binary massive black holes to merge within the Hubble time under the binary–disk interaction. We find that (1.5%<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.6%) of the total number of nearby AGNs for the equal-mass ratio and (1.3%<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.5%) for the one-to-ten mass ratio have close binary massive black holes with an orbital period of less than 10 yr in their centers, detectable with ongoing highly sensitive X-ray monitors, such as Monitor of All-sky X-ray Image and/or Swift/Burst Alert Telescope. Assuming that all binary massive black holes have the equal-mass ratio, about 10% of AGNs with black-hole masses of 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{6.5-7}\ M_{\odot}$</tex> have close binaries, and thus provide the best chance to detect them.

articleTitle: Dwarf Novae in the Shortest Orbital Period Regime: II. WZ Sge Stars as the Missing Population near the Period Minimum
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: WZ Sge-type dwarf novae are characterized by long recurrence times of outbursts (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 10 yr) and short orbital periods (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim$</tex> 85 min). A significant part of WZ Sge stars may remain undiscovered because of low outburst activity. Recently, the observed orbital period distribution of cataclysmic variables (CVs) has changed partly because outbursts of new WZ Sge stars have been discovered routinely. Hence, estimations of the intrinsic population of WZ Sge stars are important to study the population and the evolution of CVs. In this paper, we present a Bayesian approach to estimate the intrinsic period distribution of dwarf novae from observed samples. In this Bayesian model, we assumed a simple relationship between the recurrence time and the orbital period, which is consistent with observations of WZ Sge stars and other dwarf novae. As a result, the minimum orbital period was estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex> 70 min. The population of WZ Sge stars exhibited a spike-like feature at the shortest period regime in the orbital period distribution. These features are consistent with the orbital period distribution previously predicted by population synthesis studies. We propose that WZ Sge stars and CVs with a low mass-transfer rate are excellent candidates for the missing population predicted by the evolution theory of CVs.

articleTitle: Chemical Abundances of Outer Halo Stars in the Milky Way
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the chemical abundances of 57 metal-poor ([Fe/H] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< -$</tex>1) stars that are likely constituents of the outer stellar halo in the Milky Way. Almost all of the sample stars have an orbit reaching a maximum vertical distance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{\rm max}$</tex>) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 5 kpc above and below the Galactic plane. High-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \sim$</tex> 50000-55000), high signal-to-noise (S/N <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 100) spectra for the sample stars obtained with Subaru/HDS were used to derive the chemical abundances of Na, Mg, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn, Fe, Ni, Zn, Y, and Ba with an LTE abundance analysis code. The resulting abundance data were combined with those presented in the literature that mostly targeted at smaller <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{\rm max}$</tex> stars, and both data were used to investigate any systematic trends in detailed abundance patterns depending on their kinematics. It was shown that, in the metallicity range of -2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> [Fe/H] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< -$</tex>1, the [Mg/Fe] ratios for stars with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{\rm max} >$</tex> 5 kpc are systematically lower (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 0.1 dex) than those with a smaller <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{\rm max}$</tex>. For this metallicity range, a modest degree of depression in the [Si/Fe] and the [Ca/Fe] ratios was also observed. This result of lower [<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha/$</tex>Fe] for the assumed outer halo stars is consistent with previous studies that found a signature of lower [<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha/$</tex>Fe] ratios for stars with extreme kinematics. The distribution of the [Mg/Fe] ratios for the outer halo stars partly overlaps with that for stars belonging to the Milky Way dwarf satellites in the metallicity interval of -2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> [Fe/H] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< -$</tex>1 and spans a range intermediate between the distributions for the inner halo stars and the stars belonging to the satellites. Our results confirm the inhomogeneous nature of the chemical abundances within the Milky Way stellar halo, depending on the kinematic properties of the constituent stars, as suggested by earlier studies. Possible implications for the formation of the Milky Way halo and its relevance to the suggested dual nature of the halo are discussed.

articleTitle: Oscillations in G-Type Giants
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Precise radial-velocity measurements of 4 G-type giants, 11 Com, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta$</tex> Hya, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> Tau, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta$</tex> Her, were carried out. Short-term variations with amplitudes of 1–7 m s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> and periods of 3–10 hr were detected. A period analysis shows that the individual power distribution has a Gaussian shape, and that their peak frequencies (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\nu_{\rm max}$</tex>) are in a good agreement with a prediction by the scaling law. With using a pre-whitening procedure, significant frequency peaks of more than 3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \sigma$</tex> were extracted for these giants. From these peaks, we determined the large frequency separation by constructing the highest peak distribution of the collapsed power spectrum, which is also in good agreement with what the scaling law for the large separation predicts. Echelle diagrams of the oscillation frequency were created based on the extracted large separations, which is very useful to clarify the properties of the oscillation modes. In these echelle diagrams, odd-even mode sequences are clearly seen. Therefore, it is certain that in these G-type giants, non-radial modes are detected in addition to the radial mode. As a consequence, these properties of oscillation modes are shown to follow what Dziembowski et al. (2001, MNRAS, 328, 601) and Dupret et al. (2009, A&A, 506, 57) theoretically predicted. The damping times for these giants were estimated with the same method as that developed by Stello et al. (2004, Sol. Phys., 220, 207). The relation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-value (ratio of damping time to period) to the period was discussed by adding data of other stars, ranging from dwarfs to giants.

articleTitle: Japanese VLBI Network Mapping of SiO v = 3 J = 1–0 Maser Emission in W Hydrae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report first on two-epoch mapping observations of SiO <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 1–0 maser emission in the semiregular variable W Hydrae using the Japanese VLBI Network. The flux density of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 1–0 emission detected on 2009 February 28 was two orders of magnitude smaller than those of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 1 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 2 emissions, while a month and half later the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 3 flux density suddenly increased by a factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>25. In contrast, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 1 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 2 flux densities decreased during this period, as expected from the optical light curve. At the first epoch, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 3 maser features were located inside of a ring composed of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 1 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 2 features by 6 mas (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>rsim $</tex>0.5 AU) toward the central star. These offsets are meaningfully larger than the error of the fitted ring radius and the difference in the ring sizes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 1 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 2 masers (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim $</tex>0.2 AU). The present result at the first epoch suggests that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 1–0 SiO masers are predominantly excited in a pumping mechanism (e.g., collisional pumping) different from that recently proposed on the basis of the line overlap with infrared H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>O lines. Interestingly, the second-epoch observation revealed that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 3 features were located on almost the same ring as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 2 ring, which is consistent with what line-overlap theory suggests.

articleTitle: Time-Resolved Spectral Variability of the Prompt Emission from GRB 070125 Observed with Suzaku/WAM
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Time-resolved spectral analyses of GRB 070125 with significant photon detections over the MeV regime using Suzaku/WAM data are reported. The prompt emission interval was divided into 10 time regions, and their spectra were reproduced by a Band function or a cutoff power-law model. The spectra show a complex evolution; a soft-hard-soft trend is seen, rather than a typical hard-to-soft monotonic variation. In addition, a flat spectral slope in the low-energy band exceeding the slope expected from a simple synchrotron emission model is suggested in one of the time regions. These results imply that the internal shocks in the relativistic jet of GRB 070125 have different physical conditions. There is a possible excess at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex> 2.2 MeV in the spectrum of 33 seconds after the trigger at a significant level of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx $</tex>98.5%, where the continuum spectrum is not reproduced by the Band function. These properties are only shown during the short prompt time interval of the prompt emission, and emphasize the utility of the Suzaku/WAM for the study of gamma-ray bursts.

articleTitle: Trapped, Two-Armed, Nearly Vertical Oscillations in Polytropic Disks
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have examined the trapping of two-armed nearly vertical oscillations in polytropic disks. Two-armed nearly vertical oscillations are interesting in the sense that they are trapped in an inner region of disks with proper frequencies, if the inner edge of disks is a boundary that reflects oscillations. The frequencies of the trapped oscillations cover the frequency range of kHz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) to low-frequency QPOs in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs), depending on the modes of oscillations. Low-frequency trapped oscillations are particularly interesting since their trapped region is wide. These low-frequency oscillations are, however, present only when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathit{\Gamma}$</tex>(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\equiv $</tex>1 + 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$/N$</tex>) is close to, but smaller than, 4/3 (when spin parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_*$</tex> is zero), where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> is the polytropic index. The above critical value, 4/3, slightly increases as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_*$</tex> increases.

articleTitle: Dwarf Novae in the Shortest Orbital Period Regime. I A New Short Superhump Period Dwarf Nova, OT J055717+683226
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the observation of a new dwarf nova (DN), OT J055717+683226 (OT: optical transient), during the period of its first-recorded superoutburst in 2006 December. Our observation shows that this object is an SU UMa-type dwarf nova having a very short superhump period of 76.67<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.03 min (0.05324<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.00002 d). The next superoutburst was observed in 2008 March. The recurrence time of superoutbursts (supercycle) is, hence, estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>480 d. The supercycle (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 480 d) is much shorter than those (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>rsim$</tex>10 yr) of WZ Sge-type dwarf novae which are in the major of dwarf novae in the shortest orbital period regime (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim$</tex>85 min). Using a hierarchical cluster analysis, we divided the dwarf nova in the shortest orbital period regime in seven groups. We found that objects, which have short supercycles, small outburst amplitudes, and large superhump period excesses compared with those of WZ Sge stars, form a small group. OT J055717+683226 probably belongs to this group.

articleTitle: Evidence of Early Enrichment of the Galactic Disk by Large-Scale Winds
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Large-scale homogeneous surveys of Galactic stars may indicate that the elemental abundance gradient evolves with cosmic time, which is a phenomenon that was not foreseen in existing models of Galactic chemical evolution (GCE). If this phenomenon is confirmed in future studies, we can show that this effect, at least in part, is due to large-scale winds that once enriched the disk. These set up a steep abundance gradient in the inner disk (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\rm GC} \lesssim$</tex> 14 kpc). At the close of the wind phase, chemical enrichment through accretion of metal-poor material from the halo to the disk gradually reduced the metallicity of the inner region, whereas a slight increase in the metallicity proceeded beyond the solar circle. Our “wind+infall” model accounts for a flattening of the abundance gradient in the inner disk, in agreement with observations. Accordingly, we propose that enrichment by large-scale winds is a crucial factor in chemical evolution in the disk. We anticipate that rapid flattening of the abundance gradient is the hallmark of disk galaxies with significant central bulges.

articleTitle: Spectral-Lag Relations in GRB Pulses Detected with HETE-2
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Using a pulse-fit method, we investigated the spectral lags between the traditional gamma-ray band (50–400 keV) and the X-ray band (6–25 keV) for 8 GRBs with known redshifts (GRB 010921, GRB 020124, GRB 020127, GRB 021211, GRB 030528, GRB 040924, GRB 041006, and GRB 050408), detected with the WXM and FREGATE instruments aboard the HETE-2 satellite. We found several relations for individual GRB pulses between the spectral lag and other observables, such as the luminosity, pulse duration, and peak energy, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\rm peak}$</tex>. The obtained results are consistent with those for BATSE, indicating that the BATSE correlations are still valid at lower energies (6–25 keV). Furthermore, we found that the photon energy dependence for the spectral lags can be reconciled with the simple curvature effect model. We discuss the implications of these results from various points of view.

articleTitle: Spin–Orbit Alignment of the TrES-4 Transiting Planetary System and Possible Additional Radial-Velocity Variation
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report new radial velocities of the TrES-4 transiting planetary system, including observations of a full planetary transit, with the High Dispersion Spectrograph on the Subaru 8.2 m telescope. Modeling of the Rossiter–McLaughlin effect indicates that the exoplanet TrES-4b has a sky-projected angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda =$</tex> 6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex>3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm $</tex> 4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex>7 between its orbital axis and the host star’s spin one. The close spin–orbit alignment of TrES-4b seems to argue against a migration history involving planet–planet scattering or Kozai cycles, although there are two nearby faint stars that might be binary companion candidates. A comparison of our out-of-transit data from four different runs suggests that the star exhibits a radial-velocity variability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>20 m s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> in excess of a single Keplerian orbit. Although the cause of the excess variability is unknown, we discuss various possibilities such as systematic measurement errors, starspots or other intrinsic motions, and additional companions besides the transiting planet.

articleTitle: X-Ray Spectroscopy of Galactic Hot Gas along the PKS 2155-304 Sight Line
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a detailed spectroscopic study of the hot gas in the Galactic halo toward the direction of a blazer PKS 2155-304 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z =$</tex> 0.117). The O VII and O VIII absorption lines were measured with the Low and High Energy Transmission Grating Spectrographs aboard Chandra, and the O VII, O VIII, and Ne IX emission lines produced in an adjacent field of the PKS 2155-304 direction were observed with the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer aboard Suzaku. Assuming vertically exponential distributions of the gas temperature and the density, we performed a combined analysis of the absorption and emission data. The gas temperature and the density at the galactic plane were determined to be (2.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+0.6}_{-0.3}$</tex>) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{6} $</tex>K and (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.4^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$</tex>) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3} $</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3} $</tex>, and the scale heights of the gas temperature and density were 5.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+7.4}_{-4.2}$</tex> kpc and 2.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+0.9}_{-0.8}$</tex> kpc, respectively. These values are consistent with those obtained in the LMC X-3 direction.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of Mid IR / Far IR Blind, Wide Area, Spectral Surveys in Breaking the Confusion Limit
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Source confusion defines a practical depth to which to take large-area extragalactic surveys. 3D imaging spectrometers with positional as well as spectral information, however, potentially provide a means by which to use line emission to break the traditional confusion limit. In this paper we present the results of our investigation into the effectiveness of mid/far infrared, wide-area spectroscopic surveys in breaking the confusion limit. We use SAFARI, a FIR imaging Fourier Transform Spectrometer concept for the proposed JAXA-led SPICA mission, as a test case. We generate artificial skies representative of 100 SAFARI footprints and use a fully-automated redshift determination method to retrieve redshifts for both spatially and spectrally confused sources for bright-end and burst mode galaxy evolution models. We find we are able to retrieve accurate redshifts for 38/54% of the brightest spectrally confused sources, with continuum fluxes as much as an order of magnitude below the 120 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m photometric confusion limit. In addition we also recover accurate redshifts for 38/29% of the second brightest spectrally confused sources. Our results suggest that deep, spectral line surveys with SAFARI can break the traditional photometric confusion limit, and will also not only resolve, but provide redshifts for, a large number of previously inaccessible galaxies. To conclude we discuss some of the limitations of the technique, as well as further work.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observations of the Merging Cluster Abell 85: Temperature Map and Impact Direction
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: To investigate the present situation of the merging in the southern outer region of Abell 85, we carried out long-time (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 100 ks) observations with Suzaku, and produced an X-ray hardness ratio map. We found a high hardness ratio peak on the east side of a subcluster located south of the cluster; an X-ray spectrum of the region including this peak indicates a high temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 8.5 keV. This hot spot has not been reported so far. We consider that this hot spot is a postshock region produced by the infall of the subcluster from the southwest. By using the Rankine–Hugoniot jump conditions for shocks, the Mach number and the infall velocity of the subcluster were obtained as 1.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.2 and 1950<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+290}_{-280}\ $</tex>km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, respectively, in the case of merging with the subcluster from the southwest direction. By using the difference in redshift between A 85 and the subcluster obtained from optical observations, the angle between the line of sight and the direction of the motion of the subcluster is estimated to be 75<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+7^{\circ}}_{-8^\circ}$</tex>. We estimate the kinetic energy of the subcluster and the energy used for the intracluster medium (ICM) heating to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{63}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim\ $</tex>8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{60}\ $</tex>erg, respectively. This shows that the deceleration of the subcluster by the ICM heating has been negligibly small.

articleTitle: Energetic Relations between the Disappearing Solar Filaments and the Associated Flare Arcades
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the temporal and statistical relations between the mechanical energies of disappearing solar filaments and the thermal energies of the associated flare arcades in soft X-rays. Measuring the 3-D velocity fields of 10 eruptive filaments, we calculated their mechanical energy gain rate, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{\rm mc}$</tex>, per unit volume and compared it to the thermal energy release rate per unit volume, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{\rm th}$</tex>, derived with Yohkoh/SXT data. For the statistical relation, we found a relation that can be approximated as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{\rm th} \propto \epsilon_{\rm mc}^{1.9}$</tex>. This relation can be explained by interpreting the energy input to an arcade via the Poynting flux in the magnetic reconnection process and the acceleration of a filament by the Lorentz force. This explanation is also supported by the strong dependence of the observed increase rates of both the thermal and mechanical energy densities on the mean magnetic field strength of the source region. We also investigated their temporal variations, and found that the start time of increase in the mechanical energy of a filament preceded that of the thermal energy of the coronal arcade in some cases. These relations imply that the basic mechanisms that accelerate a filament and create a hot plasma are different, and both energy increase rates are determined primary by the magnetic field strengths.

articleTitle: Molecular Clouds as Cosmic-Ray Barometers
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The advent of high sensitivity, high resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray detectors, together with a knowledge of the distribution of the atomic hydrogen and especially of the molecular hydrogen in the Galaxy on a subdegree scale, creates a unique opportunity to explore the flux of cosmic rays in the Galaxy. We here present the new data on the distribution of the molecular hydrogen from a large region of the inner Galaxy obtained by the NANTEN Collaboration. We then introduce a methodology which aims to provide a test bed for current and future <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray observatories to explore the cosmic-ray flux at various positions in our Galaxy. In particular, for a distribution of molecular clouds, as provided by the NANTEN survey, and local cosmic-ray density as measured at the Earth, we estimate the expected GeV to TeV <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray signal, which can then be compared with observations, and use to test the cosmic-ray flux.

articleTitle: An Abundance Analysis of the Primary Star of the Peculiar Eclipsing Binary $\epsilon$ Aurigae out of the Eclipsing Phase
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A detailed abundance analysis of the primary star of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> Aur before an eclipse was carried out using a very high signal-to-noise ratio optical-region spectrum. An A7 Iab supergiant HD 81471, presumably a member of the Vela OB1 association, was used as a reference. We obtained atmospheric parameters (T<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{\rm eff}$</tex>, log g, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi_{\rm t}$</tex>) to be (8025 K, 1.0 and 10 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) and (8050 K, 1.0 and 7 km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> Aur and HD 81471, respectively. The abundances of Mg, Si, S, Ca, Sc, Ti, Cr, and Fe were very close to the solar abundances in both stars. Light elements C and O were under-abundant, while N and Na were over-abundant in both stars, after correcting for non-LTE effects. Definite under-abundances of Sr were detected in both stars. Slight, but definite, over-abundances were found in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> Aur for the s-process elements Y, Zr, and Ba, when compared with the results of HD 81471. Enhancements in the abundances of N, Na, and s-process elements might indicate the occurences of thermal dredge-up and the s-process nucleosynthesis in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex> Aur during the past evolution.

articleTitle: The Abundance Pattern of O, Ne, Mg, and Fe in the Interstellar Medium of S0 Galaxy NGC 4382 Observed with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We derived the O, Ne, Mg, and Fe abundances in the interstellar medium (ISM) of a relatively isolated S0 galaxy, NGC 4382, observed with the Suzaku XIS instruments, and compared the O/Ne/Mg/Fe abundance pattern with that of the ISM in elliptical galaxies. The derived temperature and Fe abundance in the ISM are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 0.3 keV and 0.6–2.9 solar, respectively. The abundance ratios are derived with considerable accuracy than the abundances, themselves; that is, the O/Fe, Ne/Fe, and Mg/Fe ratios are 0.3, 0.7, and 0.6 in solar units, respectively. The O/Fe ratio is smaller than those of the ISM in elliptical galaxies (NGC 720, NGC 1399, NGC 1404, and NGC 4636) observed with Suzaku. Since O, Ne, and Mg are predominantly synthesized by supernovae (SNe) of type II, the observed abundance pattern indicates that the contribution of SN Ia products is higher in the S0 galaxy than in the elliptical galaxy. Since the hot ISM in early-type galaxies is an accumulation of stellar mass and SN Ia products, the low O/Fe ratio in the ISM of NGC 4382 reflects a higher rate of present SNe Ia, or stars containing more SN Ia products than those in elliptical galaxies.

articleTitle: A Study of Three-Dimensional Kinematics of the Narrow-Line Region of the Seyfert Galaxy NGC 4151 Based on Integral Field Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: By using the Integral Field Spectroscopy mode of the Kyoto Tri-dimensional Spectrograph II we have mapped the two-dimensional distribution of kinematics in a wide variety of emission lines in the narrow-line region of NGC 4151. We decomposed the emission lines and defined two components: a narrow component and a broad component. The narrow component has smaller FWHM values, and is spatially more extended than the broad component. We applied a simple model to each component, a rotation in the galactic plane for the narrow component and a biconical outflow model for the broad one. The two-dimensional velocity distributions of the narrow component was well-fitted to a normal rotation in the galactic plane, with the best-fit parameters being similar among the emission lines. We found that the residual maps show similar large positive values at a knot around 6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\prime\prime}$</tex> southwest form the nucleus. For the central region, excluding the knot, the velocity field was fitted better, and the residual was small as the relative wavelength-calibration accuracy of the instrument among lenslets. We modeled the broad component with a simple biconical outflow axisymmetrical with respect to its axis by assuming a constant outflowing velocity, a constant FWHM value, and the emission line strength declining according to a power law with the distance from the nucleus. The best-fit model suggests that PA for the axis of the biconical outflow is close to the direction of the [O III] line emission elongation. Our line of sight was included within the outflowing bicone, which had filled cones.

articleTitle: Calibration of the AKARI Far-Infrared Imaging Fourier-Transform Spectrometer
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) onboard the AKARI satellite has a spectroscopic capability provided by a Fourier transform spectrometer (FIS–FTS). FIS–FTS is the first space-borne imaging FTS dedicated to far-infrared astronomical observations. We describe the calibration process of the FIS–FTS, and discuss its accuracy and reliability. The calibration is based on observational data of bright astronomical sources as well as two instrumental sources. We have compared the FIS–FTS spectra with the spectra obtained from the Long Wavelength Spectrometer (LWS) of the Infrared Space Observatory (ISO), having a similar spectral coverage. The present calibration method accurately reproduces the spectra of several solar system objects having a reliable spectral model. Under this condition the relative uncertainty of the calibration of the continuum is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 15% for SW, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 10% for 70–85 cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> of LW, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 20% for 60–70 cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> of LW; and the absolute uncertainty is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>35%/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>55% for SW, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>35%/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>55% for 70–85 cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> of LW, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>40%/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>60% for 60–70 cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> of LW. These values have been confirmed by comparisons with theoretical models and previous observations by the ISO / LWS.

articleTitle: Abundance Patterns in the Interstellar Medium of the S0 Galaxy NGC 1316 (Fornax A) Revealed with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Suzaku X-ray satellite observed the nearby S0 galaxy NGC 1316, a merger remnant aged 3 Gyr. The total good exposure time was 48.7 ks. The spectra were well represented by a two-temperature thermal model for the interstellar medium (ISM) plus a power-law model. The cool and hot temperatures of the thermal model were 0.48<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.03 and 0.92<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>0.04 keV, respectively. The excellent spectral sensitivity of Suzaku enables us for the first time to measure the metal abundances of O, Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe in the ISM. The resultant abundance pattern of O, Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe is close to that of the new solar abundance determined by Lodders (2003, ApJ, 591, 1220). The measured abundance pattern is compared with those of elliptical galaxies and an S0 galaxy, observed with Suzaku. Considering metal-enrichment from present Type Ia supernovae, the near-solar abundance pattern of the ISM in NGC 1316 indicates an enhanced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha/$</tex>Fe ratio of stellar materials in the entire galaxy, like in giant elliptical galaxies.

articleTitle: What Kinds of Accretion Disks Are There in the Nuclei of Radio Galaxies?
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: It seems to be a widely accepted opinion that the types of accretion disks (or flows) generally realized in the nuclei of radio galaxies and in further lower mass-accretion rate nuclei are inner, hot, optically thin, radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAFs) surrounded by outer, cool, optically thick, standard-type accretion disks. However, observational evidence for the existence of such outer cool disks in these nuclei is rather poor. Instead, recent observations sometime suggest the existence of inner cool disks of the non-standard type, which develop in a region very close to their central black holes. Taking NGC 4261 as a typical example of such light-eating nuclei, for which both flux data ranging from radio to X-ray and data for the counterjet occultation are available, we examine the plausibility of such a picture for the accretion states, as mentioned above, based on model predictions. It is shown that the explanation of the gap seen in the counterjet emission in terms of the free–free absorption by an outer standard disk is unrealistic and, moreover, the existence itself of such an outer standard disk seems to be very implausible. Instead, the model of RIAF in an ordered magnetic field (so-called resistive RIAF model) can well serve to explain the emission gap in terms of the synchrotron absorption, as well as to reproduce the observed features of the overall spectral energy distribution (SED). This model also predicts that the RIAF state starts directly from an interstellar hot gas phase at around the Bondi radius, and terminates at the inner edge, whose radius is about 100-times the Schwartzschild radii. Therefore, there is a good possibility for a cool disk to develop within this innermost region.

articleTitle: Subaru FOCAS Spectroscopic Observations of High-Redshift Supernovae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present spectra of high-redshift supernovae (SNe) that were taken with the Subaru low-resolution optical spectrograph, FOCAS. These SNe were found in SN surveys with Suprime-Cam on Subaru, the CFH12k camera on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope, and the Advanced Camera for Surveys on the Hubble Space Telescope. These SN surveys specifically targeted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z >$</tex> 1 Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). From the spectra of 39 candidates, we obtained redshifts for 32 candidates and spectroscopically identified 7 active candidates as probable SNe Ia, including one at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z =$</tex> 1.35, which is the most distant SN Ia to be spectroscopically confirmed with a ground-based telescope. An additional 4 candidates were identified as likely SNe Ia from the spectrophotometric properties of their host galaxies. Seven candidates are not SNe Ia, either being SNe of another type or active galactic nuclei. When SNe Ia were observed within one week of the maximum light, we found that we could spectroscopically identify most of them up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z =$</tex> 1.1. Beyond this redshift, very few candidates were spectroscopically identified as SNe Ia. The current generation of super red-sensitive, fringe-free CCDs will push this redshift limit higher.

articleTitle: On the Interpretation of the l–v Features in the Milky Way Galaxy
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We modeled the gas dynamics of barred galaxies using a three-dimensional, high-resolution, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex> hydrodynamical simulation, and applied it to the Milky Way in an attempt to reproduce both the large-scale structure and the clumpy morphology observed in galactic HI and CO <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex> diagrams. Owing to including of the multi-phase interstellar medium, self-gravity, star-formation, and supernovae feedback, the clumpy morphology, as well as the large-scale features, in observed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex> diagrams were naturally reproduced. We identified in our <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex> diagrams with a number of not only large-scale peculiar features, such as the `3-kpc arm', `135-km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> arm', and `Connecting arm', but also clumpy features, such as `Bania clumps', and then linked these features in a face-on view of our model. We give suggestions on the real structure of the Milky Way and on the fate of gas clumps in the central region.

articleTitle: Generation of Alfvén Waves by Magnetic Reconnection
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In this paper, the results of 2.5-dimensional magnetohydrodynamical simulations are reported for the magnetic reconnection of non-perfectly antiparallel magnetic fields. The magnetic field has a component perpendicular to the computational plane, that is, a guide field. The angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> between the magnetic field lines in two half regions was a key parameter in our simulations, whereas the initial distribution of the plasma was assumed to be simple; the density and pressure were uniform, except for the current sheet region. Alfvén waves were generated at the reconnection point and propagated along the reconnected field line. The energy fluxes of the Alfvén waves and the magneto-acoustic waves (slow mode and fast mode) generated by magnetic reconnection were measured. Each flux shows a similar time evolution independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>. The percentages of the energies (time integral of energy fluxes) carried by the Alfvén waves and magneto-acoustic waves to the released magnetic energy were calculated. The Alfvén waves carry 38.9%, 36.0%, and 29.5% of the released magnetic energy at the maximum (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta =$</tex> 80<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex>) in the cases of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta =$</tex> 0.1, 1, and 20, respectively, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> is the plasma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> (the ratio of gas pressure to magnetic pressure). The magneto-acoustic waves carry 16.2% (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta =$</tex> 70<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex>), 25.9% (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta =$</tex> 60<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex>), and 75.0% (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta =$</tex> 180<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex>) of the energy at the maximum. Implications of these results for solar coronal heating and acceleration of high-speed solar wind are discussed.

articleTitle: Lyman-α Emitters and Lyman-Break Galaxies at z = 3–6 in Cosmological SPH Simulations
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We study the properties of Lyman-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> emitters (LAEs) and Lyman-break galaxies (LBGs) at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3–6 using cosmological SPH simulations. We investigate two simple scenarios for explaining the observed Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> and rest-frame UV luminosity functions (LFs) of LAEs: (i) the “escape fraction” scenario, in which the effective escape fraction (including the IGM attenuation) of Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> photons is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{{\rm Ly}\alpha}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx$</tex> 0.1 (0.15) at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3 (6), and (ii) the “stochastic” scenario, in which the fraction of LAEs that are turned on at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3 (6) is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${C_{\rm stoc}}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx$</tex> 0.07 (0.2) after correcting for the IGM attenuation. Our comparisons with a number of different observations suggest that the stochastic scenario is preferred over the escape fraction scenario. We find that the mean values of stellar mass, metallicity and black hole mass hosted by LAEs are all smaller in the stochastic scenario than in the escape fraction scenario. In our simulations, the galaxy stellar mass function evolves rapidly, as expected in hierarchical structure formation. However, its evolution is largely compensated by a beginning decline in the specific star formation rate, resulting in little evolution of the rest-frame UV LF from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 6 to 3. The rest-frame UV LF of both LAEs and LBGs at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3 and 6 can be described well by the stochastic scenario provided the extinction is moderate, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx$</tex> 0.15, for both populations, although our simulation might be overpredicting the number of bright LBGs at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 6. We also discuss the correlation function and bias of LAEs. The Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> LFs at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 6 in a field-of-view of 0.2 deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> show a significantly larger scatter owing to cosmic variance relative to that in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\ $</tex>deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> field, and the scatter seen in the current observational estimates of the Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> LF can be accounted for by cosmic variance.

articleTitle: AKARI Near- to Mid-Infrared Imaging and Spectroscopic Observations of the Small Magellanic Cloud. I Bright Point Source List
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out near- to mid-infrared imaging and spectroscopic observations of patchy areas in the Small Magellanic Cloud using the Infrared Camera aboard AKARI. Two 100 arcmin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> areas were imaged in 3.2, 4.1, 7, 11, 15, and 24<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mu$</tex>m, and also spectroscopically observed in the wavelength range continuously from 2.5 to 13.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mu$</tex>m. The spectral resolving power, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/ \Delta \lambda$</tex>, values were about 20, 50, and 50 at 3.5, 6.6, and 10.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mu$</tex>m, respectively. Other than the two 100 arcmin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> areas, some patchy areas were imaged and/or spectroscopically observed as well. In this paper, we overview the observations and present a list of near- to mid-infrared photometric results, which lists <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>12000 near-infrared and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>1800 mid-infrared bright point sources detected in the observed areas. The 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \sigma$</tex> limits are 16.50, 16.12, 13.28, 11.26, 9.62, and 8.76 in Vega magnitudes at 3.2, 4.1, 7, 11, 15, and 24<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mu$</tex>m bands, respectively.

articleTitle: The Primordial Origin Model of Magnetic Fields in Spiral Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a primordial-origin model for composite configurations of global magnetic fields in spiral galaxies. We show that a uniform tilted magnetic field wound up into a rotating disk galaxy can evolve into composite magnetic configurations comprising bisymmetric spiral (S <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> BSS), axisymmetric spiral (A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> ASS), plane-reversed spiral (PR), and/or ring (R) fields in the disk, and vertical (V) fields in the center. By MHD simulations we show that these composite galactic fields are indeed created from a weak primordial uniform field, and that different configurations can co-exist in the same galaxy. We show that spiral fields trigger the growth of two-armed gaseous arms. The centrally accumulated vertical fields are twisted and produce a jet toward the halo. We found that the more vertical was the initial uniform field, the stronger was the formed magnetic field in the galactic disk.
